newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Taiwanese to close 280 factories in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Taiwanese to close 280 factories in S.Africa.

text.p: About 280 Taiwanese factories in South Africa will be closed temporarily to pressure the Pretoria government into restoring diplomatic ties with Taiwan, state television reported on Friday.

The factories, affiliated to the Association of Chinese Industrialists in Southern Africa, told television news they were uncertain about their future in South Africa and needed diplomatic offices to protect them.
South African President Nelson Mandela announced in November last year that Pretoria, easily the biggest of Taiwan's diplomatic allies, would switch ties to mainland China this year.

The price of relations with Beijing is abandonment of ties with Taiwan, which China has regarded as a rebel province since a civil war split them in 1949. Beijing seeks to isolate Taiwan diplomatically in its quest for sovereignty over the island.
Nearly 300 Taiwan businesses have operations in South Africa with total investment topping $1.5 billion. At least 43,000 jobs are created through Taiwanese investment.

The tie-switching announcement by South Africa was a big blow to Taiwan, which now has only 29 minor diplomatic allies. Its relations with Taiwan date back to the apartheid era when both were diplomatic pariahs.
